response.sql: WITH joined_data AS (SELECT s.questregistry, s.gbsize, s.spanmin, st.zoneregistry, st.riskeval FROM scans s INNER JOIN sites st ON s.zoneref = st.zoneregistry), group_rates AS (SELECT riskeval, AVG(gbsize / spanmin) as group_rate FROM joined_data WHERE gbsize IS NOT NULL AND spanmin IS NOT NULL AND spanmin > 0 GROUP BY riskeval), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(group_rate) as benchmark_rate FROM group_rates), filtered_groups AS (SELECT gr.group_rate, b.benchmark_rate FROM group_rates gr CROSS JOIN benchmark b WHERE b.benchmark_rate IS NOT NULL AND gr.group_rate > b.benchmark_rate) SELECT AVG(group_rate) as avg_rate, AVG(group_rate - benchmark_rate) as avg_excess FROM filtered_groups;

assumptions.assumption: Scans where the GB-per-minute ratio is 'missing' includes not only NULL values for gbsize or spanmin, but also cases where spanmin is zero or negative. This prevents division-by-zero errors and ensures mathematically valid ratios. The request says 'ignoring scans where that ratio is missing' without explicitly defining 'missing'.

alternatives.interpretation: Only ignore scans where gbsize or spanmin is NULL, permitting spanmin = 0. Division behavior varies by SQL dialect: PostgreSQL raises an error, MySQL returns NULL (which AVG() skips). This interpretation assumes database-specific null-handling rather than defensive filtering.
